summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution.
takeaways: In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos.
On test videos containing mistakes, both designs outperform released AEM and ESTANet checkpoints under our evaluation protocol.

Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the video ends.
